candidate_sentences.text: Eleving Group delivered record financial performance in 2024, supported by strong portfolio growth, higher demand and improved operational efficiency.
Revenue increased nearly 15% to EUR 216.6 million from EUR 189.3 million in 2023, while adjusted EBITDA rose more than 16% to EUR 89.8 million from EUR 77.5 million.
Total net profit reached an all-time high of EUR 29.6 million, up almost 21% from EUR 24.5 million.
Loan issuance increased 26.8% to EUR 368.6 million, and the net loan and pre-owned vehicle rental portfolio grew 16% to EUR 371.2 million from EUR 320.3 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Key year-over-year improvements included a 29.3% capitalization ratio (vs 26.1% in 2023), 2.4 interest coverage ratio (vs 2.3), and reduced net leverage to 3.3x (from 3.7x).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report financial highlights; Note 48 Alternative Performance Measures

candidate_sentences.text: Total equity increased to EUR 108.1 million from EUR 65.4 million, the capitalization ratio improved to 29.3% from 26.1%, and net leverage declined to 3.3 from 3.7.

verified_key_information_units.information: Major performance drivers were organic growth in Europe/Africa, successful integration of Sub-Saharan operations (tripling regional portfolio), digital transformation (doubled applications, new self-service platform), and enhanced risk management improving portfolio quality.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO keynote; Management report operations section

candidate_sentences.text: Demand was supported by digitalization, expanded sales channels and the completion of the Sub-Saharan integration; the combined portfolio in the Group’s three main Sub-Saharan markets tripled during the year.

Sustainability and product development also advanced, including financing more than 2,000 electric motorcycles in East Africa.

verified_key_information_units.information: Business segments showed vehicle finance (67% of portfolio: 45% traditional, 20% flexible/subscription) and consumer finance (33%: Kredo, Tigo, etc.), with key growth in East Africa (e-motorcycles), Romania, Uganda, and Albania offsetting exits from Balkan/Belarus.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report segments; Sustainability statement portfolio balance; Note 19 discontinued operations

verified_key_information_units.information: Capital structure transformed via October 2024 IPO raising EUR 29.0 mln equity (largest in Nasdaq Riga history), used to repay subordinated bonds and high-cost Mintos loans, while expanding local currency funding (Kenya +30%, Botswana notes).

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K3, and K5 are fully present with supporting sentences. K6 is partially present as it mentions electric motorcycles and product development but lacks details on geographic expansion and ESG strategy timelines. K4 is missing entirely as there is no mention of business segments, regional growth offsets, or specific product mix details. K7 is missing as there are no references to post-reporting period events like the March 2025 bond tap or tax refund.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. All statements are logically connected and support the overall narrative of strong financial performance in 2024. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, or organizational problems. The summary flows logically from revenue and profit growth to specific line items, portfolio quality improvements, capital structure changes, and future plans. While there is a mention of a one-off expense (S4), it is clearly presented as an adjustment and does not create contradictions. The relationships between financial metrics (e.g., interest expense as a proportion of interest revenue in S6) are consistent and well-explained. The summary avoids unnecessary repetition and maintains a clear, cohesive structure.
